entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Umesh Chandra Shukla,Abhishek Kumar Jaiswal

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

Heard Sri Abhishek Kumar Jaiswal, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Ms. Ifra Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
2.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 68 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468 IPC, Police Station Lohta, District Varuna (Commissionerate Varanasi), with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

3. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have objected to the mutation proceedings undertaken by the Revenue Department, as such, had demanded Rs. 2 lakhs as ransom to remove the objections.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in Sadanand Singh vs State Of U.P.And 2 Others on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158620795/
1 the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.

entities.text: Sadanand Singh vs State Of U.P.And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned counsel has next stated that no amount has been transferred for demanding the ransom.
There is no caste certificate on record.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgement of the Apex Court.
8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.text: Sadanand Singh vs State Of U.P.And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
